expectations.text: Frames a first dedicated platform hire at this company as a real resourcing shift rather than a routine backfill
expectations.evidence: The document says the API is a 'bolt-on' that is 'run by two backend engineers part-time'. It flags a 'Sizing risk' because 'three specialized hires on top of two part-time engineers is above that norm', and it recommends gating the Partner Engineer search. The PM mission is to 'Turn Calder's public REST API from an enterprise-driven side project into a product'. Together these imply a real resourcing shift, but the document never says outright that these are the first dedicated hires and not a backfill, and it never discusses what that shift means for the organization beyond reporting lines a

expectations.text: Any scorecard produced lists quantified outcomes rather than vague responsibilities such as owning the platform
expectations.evidence: All three scorecards list dated, measurable outcomes. Examples: 'Day 60: an instrumented baseline is live', 'at least 10 interviews', 'at least 80% of committed roadmap items', 'active API accounts reach at least 2x the day-60 baseline', 'SLO 99.9%', 'cut by at least 50% from the day-30 baseline', 'Zero unannounced breaking changes', 'cut by 30% from baseline by day 180', and 'at least 5 qualified partners... at least 2 live integrations'. No outcome is a vague responsibility like 'own the platform'.

expectations.text: Frames a first dedicated platform hire at this company as a real resourcing shift rather than a routine backfill
expectations.evidence: Some framing points this way. The PM mission is to 'Turn the REST API from an accommodation for three accounts into a product'. An assumption states the hires 'add product, architecture and partner capacity, and they don't replace those engineers.' The Architect mission aims to shrink 'the 2-engineer maintenance burden.' Still, the transcript never says outright that this is the company's first dedicated platform investment. It also doesn't spell out what changes organizationally (ownership, budget, strategy). The shift is implied, not stated.

expectations.text: Any scorecard produced lists quantified outcomes rather than vague responsibilities such as owning the platform
expectations.evidence: All three scorecards use ranked, time-bound outcomes instead of responsibilities. Examples: 'Within 60 days, publish a written API strategy...', 'at least 15 API consumers', '2 reference integrations', 'zero unannounced breaking changes', 'at most [X]% of their time on API maintenance'. Several targets are still placeholders ([X]%, [N] partners, [baseline]→[target]), so many outcomes have a measurable shape but no actual number yet.
